'''Franz Mandl''' (1923–2009) was a British [[theoretical physicist]], known for his graduate-level textbooks.

== Early life and education ==
Mandl was born in [[Vienna]] in 1923 into a Jewish family. They moved to [[Berlin]] in the 1920s, and after the [[rise of Nazi Germany]], the family emigrated to England as refugees in 1936. Mandl received a scholarship to study at [[Lincoln College, Oxford]] where he received his undergraduate and doctorate degrees in physics.<ref name=guardian>{{cite news |first=Geoffrey |last=Taylor |date=25 May 2009 |title=Obituary: Franz Mandl |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/theguardian/2009/may/25/franz-mandl |access-date=27 May 2020}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
After receiving his doctorate, Mandl spent a few years in the US, before returning to the UK to become a reader of physics at the [[University of Manchester]]. He spent his career there collaborating in atomic research and writing textbooks.<ref name=guardian/> His books were considered influential to the graduate study of theoretical physics.<ref name=iop>{{cite journal |first=P D B |last=Collins |year=1985 |journal=Physics Bulletin |publisher=[[Institute of Physics]] |volume=36 |pages=391 |title=Book reviews: Quantum Field Theory |doi=10.1088/0031-9112/36/9/028}}</ref><ref name=contempphys>{{cite journal |first=D |last=Bailin |year=2009 |journal=[[Contemp. Phys.]] |volume=51 |issue=2 |pages=182–183 |title=Book reviews: Modern Quantum Field Theory: A Concise Introduction, by T. Banks |doi=10.1080/00107510903073286|s2cid=122763918 }}</ref>

== Personal life and death ==
Mandl married Betty Clifford, a mathematician whom he met while studying at Oxford.<ref name=guardian/>

He died in 2009 at the age of 85.<ref name=guardian/>
